This pathway suggests that Bremelanotide may exert its effects through a mechanism involving the FcRn receptor, which is known to play a role in the degradation of immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the liver. The involvement of hepatocytes, the primary cell type in the liver, implies that Bremelanotide could influence liver function or immune responses by targeting this receptor. The evidence points to a potential role of Bremelanotide in modulating hepatic processes, possibly through the FcRn pathway, although the exact mechanism of action remains to be fully elucidated.
